rules.title: Anti-retaliation protection and six-month reprisal presumption (M.G.L. c. 186 § 18)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not threaten or take reprisals against residential tenants for protected activity, such as reporting code violations, bringing legal actions, or joining a tenants' union. A termination notice (except for nonpayment of rent), rent increase, or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of that activity is presumed to be a reprisal, which the landlord can rebut only by clear and convincing evidence.
rules.key_value: 6-month rebuttable presumption; damages 1-3 months' rent or actual damages, whichever is greater
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenants of residential premises in Massachusetts who engage in protected activity. Protected activity includes legal or administrative enforcement actions, code-violation reports, written complaints to the landlord, tenants' union organizing, and rent payments to a unit owners' organization under c. 183A § 6(c).
rules.exemptions: Notices of termination for nonpayment of rent are excluded from the presumption.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when the tenant (or another person on the tenant's behalf or relating to the building) engaged in protected activity within the prior six months.

rules.penalty: Damages of not less than one month's rent or more than three months' rent, or the tenant's actual damages, whichever is greater, plus costs of suit and reasonable attorney's fees; any lease waiver is void.
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.
rules.conflict_note: This is an anti-retaliation statute, not a general just-cause eviction requirement. It is categorized under just_cause_eviction as the closest fit because it restricts terminations and rent increases after protected activity. Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause requirement in this document. The document does not state an effective date.
